title: Many Names
bigQuestion: Why do martial arts from different places have different names?

story.title: Six Names on One Sign
story.kicker: A hallway sign lists six arts, and each name comes from a different place.
paragraphs: A community center has a long hallway. At the end hangs a sign with six names on it. Judo. Karate. Taekwondo. Kung fu. Muay Thai. Capoeira.
A girl named Rosa reads the sign slowly. She thinks they might be one family. But the names do not match at all. Each name comes from a different language.

Her grandpa points to each one. Judo is a Japanese word. Karate grew on Okinawa. Taekwondo is Korean. Kung fu is an English way to say a Chinese word. Muay Thai is from Thailand. Capoeira is from Brazil.
Rosa smiles. The sign is like a map. Each name tells her where an art began and what language its people speak. Six names point to six places.
story.think: Can you name a food or a game whose name comes from another language?

lessons.title: Judo Means the Gentle Way
lessons.mainIdea: Judo is a Japanese name that means the gentle way.
reading: Judo is a Japanese word with two parts. Ju means gentle or soft. *Do* means way or path. So judo means the gentle way.
Kanō Jigorō chose this name for his school in Tokyo. Many other arts from Japan end in do too. Kendo is the way of the sword. It uses bamboo swords and armor.
Sumo is also from Japan. It is much older than judo. Today the Japan Sumo Association runs the big sumo contests.

words.d: a Japanese and Korean word part meaning way or path
a Japanese art with bamboo swords and armor; its name means the way of the sword

look.title: Words That End the Same
look.text: Look at three names written on cards: judo, kendo, aikido. Each one ends with the same two letters. All three come from Japan. The end part, do, means way.
look.prompt: What part of each name is the same, and what does it mean?

check.q: What does judo mean?
check.why: Ju means gentle and do means way. So judo means the gentle way.

check.q: What does do mean in names like judo and kendo?
check.why: Do means way or path.

check.q: Which art uses bamboo swords and armor?
check.why: Kendo, the way of the sword, uses bamboo swords and armor.

lessons.title: Karate From Okinawa
lessons.mainIdea: Karate grew on Okinawa, and its name came to mean empty hand.
reading: The islands of Okinawa were once the Ryukyu Kingdom. The kingdom traded with China for hundreds of years. In 1879, Japan took over the islands.
Karate grew on Okinawa. At first, its name was written to mean China hand. In the 1930s, teachers began to write it a new way. The new way means *empty hand*.
Karate spread to Japan, and then the world. It was in the Olympics for the first time at the Tokyo Games, held in 2021.

words.d: the old kingdom on the Okinawa islands, before Japan took over in 1879
the meaning of the word karate as it has been written since the 1930s

look.title: One Name, Two Ways to Write It
look.text: Picture a teacher at a board. She writes the sound kara-te two ways. Under the first way she writes China hand. Under the second way she writes empty hand. The sound stays the same.
look.prompt: How can one name be spoken the same but mean two things?

check.q: What was Okinawa before 1879?
check.why: Okinawa was the Ryukyu Kingdom until Japan took over in 1879.

check.q: What does karate mean, as written since the 1930s?
check.why: Since the 1930s, karate has been written to mean empty hand.

check.q: When was karate first in the Olympics?
choices: at the Tokyo Games held in 2021
check.why: Karate was first in the Olympics at the Tokyo Games, held in 2021.

sections.title: Names From Korea, China and Thailand

lessons.title: Taekwondo From Korea
lessons.mainIdea: Taekwondo is a Korean art, and it is not the same as karate.
reading: *Taekwondo* comes from Korea. The name has three parts. Tae means foot. Kwon means fist. Do means way, just as in Japanese.
The name taekwondo was chosen in Korea in 1955. Karate and taekwondo are different arts. They come from different lands, with different languages and different rule books.
Taekwondo was shown at the 1988 Olympics in Seoul, Korea. It became a full Olympic sport with medals in 2000, in Sydney, Australia.

words.d: a martial art and sport from Korea; its name joins foot, fist and way

look.title: Two Cards, Two Countries
look.text: Look at two cards on a table. One says karate, Okinawa, Japanese words. The other says taekwondo, Korea, Korean words. Both have a picture of a white uniform and a black belt.
look.prompt: The uniforms look alike. What makes the two arts different?

check.q: Where does taekwondo come from?
check.why: Taekwondo is a Korean art. Karate grew on Okinawa.

check.q: When did taekwondo become a full Olympic sport with medals?
check.why: It was shown in 1988 and became a medal sport in 2000, in Sydney.

check.q: Are karate and taekwondo the same art?
choices: Yes, they are two names for one art.
No, they come from different lands and languages.
check.why: Karate grew on Okinawa and taekwondo in Korea. They are different arts.

lessons.title: Kung Fu Is a Wide Word
lessons.mainIdea: Kung fu is a wide English word for many different Chinese martial arts.
reading: *Kung fu* is an English way to say a Chinese word. In Chinese, the word can mean any skill that takes hard work and time. A great cook can have kung fu too.
China is a huge country with many regions. It has hundreds of martial arts styles, not one. Tai chi and wing chun are two of them. In China, many people call these arts *wushu*.
The words kung fu became well known in English in the 1970s. Films and TV shows spread them.

words.d: an English word for many Chinese martial arts; in Chinese it means skill from hard work
a Chinese word for martial arts

look.title: A Big Umbrella
look.text: Picture a big umbrella with the words kung fu on it. Under it stand many small signs. One says tai chi. One says wing chun. Many more signs fill the space. Each sign is its own style.
look.prompt: Why is kung fu called a wide word?

check.q: What can kung fu mean in Chinese?
choices: a skill from hard work and time
check.why: In Chinese, the word means a skill that takes hard work and time.

check.q: How many martial arts styles does China have?
check.why: China has hundreds of styles, like tai chi and wing chun.

check.q: What do many people in China call martial arts?
check.why: Wushu is a Chinese word for martial arts.

lessons.title: Muay Thai From Thailand
lessons.mainIdea: Muay Thai is the national sport of Thailand, and muay means boxing.
reading: Muay Thai comes from Thailand. In the Thai language, *muay* means boxing. So Muay Thai means Thai boxing.
Muay Thai is called the national sport of Thailand. Big stadiums in Bangkok hold matches many nights of the week. Lumpinee and Rajadamnern are two famous ones.
Before a match, many fighters honor their teachers with a slow ceremony. It is called the *wai khru*. Wai means to show respect. Khru means teacher.

words.d: a ceremony before a Muay Thai match that honors teachers

look.title: A Thank-You Before the Match
look.text: Look at a ring under bright lights in Bangkok. Music plays. A fighter moves slowly around the ring, alone. He is thanking his teachers before the match. The crowd waits quietly.
look.prompt: Why might someone thank a teacher before a big day?

check.q: What does muay mean in Thai?
check.why: Muay is the Thai word for boxing.

check.q: What is the wai khru?
check.why: The wai khru is a ceremony that honors teachers before a match.

check.q: In which city are the Lumpinee and Rajadamnern stadiums?
check.why: Lumpinee and Rajadamnern are famous Muay Thai stadiums in Bangkok.

sections.title: Names From Islands, Brazil and Europe

lessons.title: Arnis and Silat
lessons.mainIdea: Arnis comes from the Philippines, and pencak silat comes from Indonesia and nearby lands.
reading: *Arnis* comes from the Philippines. It is also called eskrima or kali. It is known for its sticks. In 2009, a Philippine law named arnis the country's national martial art and sport.
*Pencak silat* comes from Indonesia and nearby lands, like Malaysia. There are many styles on many islands. In 2019, UNESCO honored pencak silat as part of the world's heritage.

words.d: a martial art from the Philippines, also called eskrima or kali
martial arts from Indonesia and nearby lands, with many styles

look.title: Three Names, One Art
look.text: Look at a poster from the Philippines. At the top it says arnis. Under that it says eskrima. Under that it says kali. A pair of rattan sticks is drawn below the words.
look.prompt: Why might one art have three different names?

check.q: Where does arnis come from?
check.why: Arnis, also called eskrima or kali, comes from the Philippines.

check.q: What did a Philippine law do in 2009?
choices: It named arnis the national martial art and sport.
It put arnis in the Olympics.
check.why: A 2009 law named arnis the national martial art and sport.

check.q: Who honored pencak silat in 2019?
check.why: UNESCO honored pencak silat as world heritage in 2019.

lessons.title: Old Names From Europe
lessons.mainIdea: Fencing, boxing and wrestling from Europe were in the Olympics long before judo or taekwondo.
reading: Europe gave its own names to its arts. Many fencing words are French. Boxing rules grew in England. Capoeira, from Brazil, has a Portuguese name.
*Greco-Roman wrestling* has a name that sounds very old. But the style took shape in France in the 1800s. People named it to honor old Greece and Rome.
Fencing and wrestling were in the first modern Olympics in 1896. Boxing joined in 1904. Judo came in 1964, and taekwondo in 2000.

words.d: a style of wrestling that took shape in France in the 1800s, named for old Greece and Rome
world games held every four years; the modern Olympics began in 1896

look.title: First Year in the Olympics
look.unit: year of first Olympic medal event
look.prompt: Which art joined the Olympics most recently?

check.q: Where did Greco-Roman wrestling take shape?
check.why: The name honors Greece and Rome, but the style took shape in France in the 1800s.

check.q: When did boxing join the Olympics?
check.why: Boxing joined the Olympics in 1904.

check.q: Which language gave many fencing words?
check.why: Many fencing words, like piste, are French.

review.why: Taekwondo is Korean. Karate grew on Okinawa.

choices: a wide English word for many Chinese arts
review.why: Kung fu covers many Chinese styles, like tai chi and wing chun.

review.q: What does karate mean, as written today?
review.why: Since the 1930s, karate has been written to mean empty hand.
Muay Thai, or Thai boxing, comes from Thailand.

review.q: What language is the word capoeira?
review.why: Capoeira comes from Brazil, where people speak Portuguese.

review.q: What are two other names for arnis?
review.why: In the Philippines, arnis is also called eskrima or kali.
